title: Add OpenTelemetry wiring (traces + metrics) + log correlation; Console deep-link examples
author: Sabrina James
body: Title: Add OpenTelemetry wiring (traces + metrics) + log correlation; Console deep-link examples Context: Quickstart templates need a consistent “production shape” for traces/metrics/log correlation across languages so that (a) the Redwood Console can attribute latency/cost to routes/models/tenants and (b) support can debug issues (timeouts/429s/streaming disconnects) using request_id + trace_id. This PR adds the baseline OpenTelemetry plumbing to the Python (FastAPI) and TypeScript (Express/Next route) templates and standardizes correlation fields in structured logs. It also adds small examples showing how to generate Redwood Console deep links (trace + request view) from emitted IDs. Scope: - Tracing: create a server span per inbound request; propagate W3C trace context (traceparent) to Redwood API calls; add required span attributes per telemetry contract v1. - Metrics: emit low-cardinality counters/histograms for request count, latency, token usage, and error classification, with consistent metric names and attribute keys. - Logs: ensure every log line includes correlation identifiers (request_id, trace_id, span_id) + tenancy tags (tenant_id when present) and route/model tags where available, while keeping cardinality controls (no raw prompts, no doc IDs, no user-provided strings). - Docs/examples: README snippets for enabling OTLP export locally (collector optional), and “Console deep link” helper functions for both languages. Notable implementation details (high level): - Python: - Added OpenTelemetry SDK init via a single function init_telemetry(service_name, env) that configures resource attributes, trace provider, meter provider, and OTLP exporters. - FastAPI middleware sets request_id (incoming x-request-id or generated UUIDv4), attaches it to response headers, and stores it in contextvars so logs and downstream calls can pick it up. - Instrumented Redwood SDK calls by injecting trace context and ensuring we set redwood.request_id on outbound headers for server-side echoing. - Metrics: http.server.duration histogram, http.server.requests counter, redwood.tokens.input/output counters, redwood.request.cost_usd histogram (optional; only if cost is returned by API). - TypeScript: - Added a shared telemetry bootstrap that configures @opentelemetry/sdk-node with OTLP exporters and AsyncLocalStorage-based context propagation. - Express middleware generates/propagates x-request-id and sets it on res; adds active span attributes from the telemetry contract. - Wrapped Redwood client calls to attach trace context and include the request_id header; also attaches model/route tags when known. - Metrics: same naming as Python; uses @opentelemetry/api-metrics with explicit views to keep boundaries stable. Telemetry contract alignment: This PR follows quickstart-telemetry-contract-v1: required attributes include (where applicable) redwood.request_id, redwood.tenant_id, redwood.route, redwood.model, redwood.deployment_mode, redwood.error_class, http.method, http.route, http.status_code, server.address, server.port. Cardinality guardrails: - http.route uses route templates (e.g., /v1/chat) not raw paths. - tenant_id is optional and expected to be a bounded set (template default: “local-dev” unless explicitly set). - No prompt strings, user IDs, doc titles, or tool args are logged or added as span attributes. - Error messages are truncated to 512 chars and classified into error_class enums (timeout | rate_limited | upstream_5xx | invalid_request | auth | network | unknown). Console deep links: Added docs + helpers showing how to log links to the Console using the trace_id and request_id; this does not hardcode a single URL, but uses REDWOOD_CONSOLE_BASE_URL and composes stable paths. Example (TypeScript): console.info({ request_id, trace_id }, `Console trace: ${consoleBase}/traces/${trace_id}`); Example (Python): logger.info("console_trace_url=%s", f"{console_base}/traces/{trace_id}") Changed areas/files (representative): - templates/python/common/telemetry.py (new) - templates/python/common/logging.py (updated structured logging + correlation) - templates/python/rag-service/app.py (middleware wiring + span attrs) - templates/typescript/common/telemetry.ts (new) - templates/typescript/common/logger.ts (adds trace_id/span_id fields) - templates/typescript/rag-service/server.ts (middleware + outbound header propagation) - docs/observability.md (new: local OTLP setup + Console links) - .env.example (adds OTEL_* and REDWOOD_CONSOLE_BASE_URL) How to test: - Local: set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318 (or use the no-op exporter by omitting OTEL_*), run the template, curl /healthz and /v1/chat, verify logs include request_id + trace_id and that spans show up in your collector. - Smoke: run the included scripts to produce a few requests and confirm counters/histograms are emitted (look for metric names starting with http.server.* and redwood.*). CI: - 2026-01-13: CI failed initially on TypeScript lint (unused import in telemetry.ts) and Python mypy (missing type hints on contextvar); fixed in 2 follow-up commits. - 2026-01-15: CI green (lint, typecheck, unit tests, template build). Commit summary: 1) Add shared OTEL bootstrap for Python templates 2) Add shared OTEL bootstrap for TypeScript templates 3) Add request_id propagation + response echo header 4) Add structured log correlation fields (trace_id/span_id) 5) Add metrics instruments + stable views/buckets 6) Docs: OTLP local setup + Console deep link snippets Review notes / discussion: - Logan Wright: Requested aligning metric/attribute keys with the contract, and explicitly documenting which attributes are optional vs required; also asked to avoid adding user-controlled values as span attrs. Addressed by: renaming tenant field to redwood.tenant_id, ensuring http.route uses templates, and adding a short “Cardinality + PII” section to docs/observability.md. - Allison Grant: Asked for a single entry point function for telemetry init (avoid per-template divergence) and to ensure shutdown hooks flush exporters. Addressed by: init_telemetry() wrappers in both languages and adding graceful shutdown flush calls in app lifecycle. - Nadia Rahman: Confirmed cost metric should be optional and not computed client-side; asked to prefer server-returned token usage and cost if available. Addressed by: token/cost emission is gated on presence in response metadata; otherwise only request/latency metrics are emitted. - Sean Gallagher: Requested defaults that don’t spam logs when exporter is misconfigured; also asked for a clear error taxonomy mapping (especially for 429 and timeouts). Addressed by: exporter init is best-effort with a one-time warning; error_class mapping added with explicit 429 => rate_limited and timeout => timeout. Merge: Squash merged to main on 2026-01-16 by Sabrina James. Release note: Templates now emit OTEL traces/metrics with standardized correlation fields and include docs for Console deep linking to traces/requests.
